name: Swarm Intelligence
description: Computational intelligence inspired by collective behavior of social insects, flocking birds, and schooling fish. Decentralized agents following simple local rules produce globally coherent, adaptive behavior. Bridges biological swarm patterns (bee, ant) with distributed AI architectures.

core_attributes.architecture: decentralized multi-agent with local interaction rules

training_paradigm: decentralized local-rule iteration converging to global optima

scope.definition: Optimization accuracy of PSO on standard continuous optimization benchmarks — fraction of 30-dimensional CEC2014 functions where PSO finds within 1% of global optimum in 100,000 function evaluations.

evidence.source: Kennedy & Eberhart (1995) 'Particle swarm optimization', ICNN; Zhan et al. (2009) 'Adaptive particle swarm optimization', IEEE Transactions on Systems.
cross_domain_examples: PSO achieves 0.88 convergence rate on unimodal CEC2014 functions vs 0.72 for GA at equivalent budget
cognitive+social velocity update combines personal best and global best — distributed gradient estimation
ant colony optimization: analogous pheromone-based distributed search converging to near-optimal paths

scope.falsifiability: If random search with equal function evaluations achieves statistically equivalent global optimum proximity to PSO on CEC2014 benchmarks, PSO velocity dynamics provide no search advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: PSO performance degrades on multimodal functions without diversity preservation mechanisms. Premature convergence to local optima is the primary failure mode. Performance is sensitive to inertia weight schedule.

scope.definition: Tour quality of ACO on traveling salesman problem — ratio of ACO best tour length to Concorde exact optimum across 50 benchmark instances with 50-500 nodes.

evidence.source: Dorigo & Gambardella (1997) 'Ant colony system', IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 1:53-66; Stützle & Hoos (2000) 'MAX-MIN ant system', Future Generation Computer Systems.
cross_domain_examples: MAX-MIN Ant System achieves 0.85-0.95 ratio of optimal TSP tour quality across TSPLIB benchmarks
ACO for network routing (OSPF): 0.88 congestion reduction vs static routing on dynamic traffic networks
biological ant pheromone system: the physical inspiration for ACO — achieves 0.96 optimality in controlled experiments

scope.falsifiability: If ACO tour lengths are statistically equivalent to nearest-neighbor heuristic on the same TSP instances, pheromone-mediated information sharing provides no benefit over greedy local heuristic.
scope.measurement_limits: ACO quality-time tradeoff depends on pheromone evaporation rate. Too-slow evaporation causes stagnation on suboptimal tours. Computational TSP performance lags biological ant colonies by 10-15% on equivalent problem sizes.

scope.definition: Speed-accuracy tradeoff efficiency of swarm consensus algorithms — time to consensus (as fraction of maximum possible time) at target decision accuracy (90%) on binary choice tasks across 100-agent simulations.

evidence.source: Valentini et al. (2016) 'Collective decision with 100 kilobots', Swarm Intelligence 10:99-112; Reina et al. (2018) 'Psychophysical laws and the superorganism', Scientific Reports 8:4387.
cross_domain_examples: Kilobot swarm (100 robots): reaches 90% consensus on quality-difference tasks in 0.83 of possible speed
voter model: theoretical consensus time O(N log N) — swarm algorithms achieve O(log N) via local amplification
honeybee swarm site selection: quorum-based consensus with 0.92 site-quality discrimination accuracy

scope.falsifiability: If 100-agent swarms using consensus algorithms show no faster convergence than fully independent voting on quality-discrimination tasks, inter-agent communication provides no collective decision advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Consensus speed-accuracy tradeoff is population-size dependent — larger swarms are slower but more accurate. Communication noise reduces both speed and accuracy. Results from simulation may not transfer to physical robot swarms.
